content.text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl-4-carboxamide. One phenyl ring carries SO2NH2 at the ortho position and is joined to a para-substituted phenyl ring. That second ring carries C(=O)NH-.

The NH is attached to a central benzene ring. Next to the NH carbon, the ring has a C(=O)NH-(5-bromopyridin-2-yl) group. Fluorine sits para to the NH carbon.

Central ring numbering: C1 bears the NH, C2 bears the carboxamide, C3 is CH, C4 bears F, C5 is CH and C6 is CH. In the drawing, the top-left carbon (NH) connects to the top-right CH, then to the right carbon, and then to the F-bearing carbon at the lower right. The lower-left carbon bears the C(=O). The ring runs: C1 (NH, top-left), C6 (top, upper right), C5 (right, upper), C4 (F, lower right), C3 (bottom, CH), C2 (C=O, left).

The F carbon is therefore separated from C2 by one CH, which puts F meta to the carboxamide. It is separated from C1 by two CH carbons, which puts F para to the NH carbon.

The pyridine ring has N adjacent to the carbon bonded to the NH. Br is at the 5-position, which is para to the NH-bearing C2 position, matching the drawing.

SMILES for the central ring: c1(NC(=O)...)ccc(F)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Br)cn1

Full SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1-c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(F)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Br)cn1

SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1-c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(F)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Br)cn1
